How to compare AI security controls

A risk register, a content filter and a runtime inspection tool answer different questions. Map your data path first, then buy the control that covers the gap.

Three AI security tools to test at different layers

A security review can cover prompts, model responses and request logs. Buying one control does not answer all three questions. Choose the layer that owns the risk, then test it with synthetic examples your reviewers can share with the vendor.

We chose these examples for the specific work documented in a client case or product guide. Client outcomes are provider-reported. AY Automate publishes this guide.

  1. Google Cloud Model Armor · Screen prompts and responses

    Google documents Model Armor as a screening layer for model inputs and outputs. Prepare a benign support request and a version containing synthetic sensitive data. Record which rule fires, what the caller receives and whether your application can handle the decision without exposing the original input.

    Read the source from Google Cloud Model Armor

  2. Amazon Bedrock Guardrails · Apply a policy to model interactions

    AWS documents configurable safeguards in Bedrock Guardrails. Have the policy owner label a small set of acceptable and unacceptable responses before the trial. Compare those labels with the observed decisions. A useful review includes the legitimate questions that were blocked and the extra work that created for staff.

    Read the source from Amazon Bedrock Guardrails

  3. Cloudflare AI Gateway · Inspect traffic through a gateway

    Cloudflare documents observability for model requests through AI Gateway. Trace one synthetic request from the application through the gateway and back. Check which fields an operator can read, how long they persist and whether turning off a log affects your ability to investigate a failed request.

    Read the source from Cloudflare AI Gateway

What to ask before you buy

  1. Draw where prompts, files and responses go, including logs, backups and subprocessors.
  2. Test the proposed policy with a synthetic sensitive record. Check the audit event and who can read it.
  3. Exercise an outage and a deletion request. Record what fails closed and what remains in storage.

How to compare prices

Request separate estimates for inspections, log storage, governance seats and implementation. Estimate the cost of retaining evidence for your required audit period.

A worked example to review

Cisco publishes an AI Defense reference architecture for its AI PODs. Use the architecture to compare inspection points with your own model deployment.

Read the provider’s example

Does buying a guardrail make an AI deployment compliant?

A guardrail covers a specific interaction. Your team still needs to establish lawful access, retention, review ownership and evidence for its applicable requirements.
